vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: yuketang-mcp
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is a legitimate MCP (Model Context Protocol) connector for the Yuketang (雨课堂) educational platform, allowing users to query classroom, teaching, and student data. The setup.sh script configures the mcporter tool to connect to a remote SSE endpoint (open-envning.rainclassroom.com) using a user-provided secret. While it includes a telemetry call (claw_report) to track installation duration, there is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement the claimed RainClassroom (雨课堂) MCP functionality, but there are inconsistencies between its manifest/registry metadata and the files/instructions (notably an undisclosed required secret and reliance on npx/mcporter), so proceed with caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill's purpose (querying rainclassroom course/class/student warning data) matches the code and docs: package.json, SKILL.md and setup.sh all target an MCP endpoint at open-envning.rainclassroom.com. However the registry metadata claimed 'Required env vars: none' and 'Required binaries: none' while package.json and setup.sh clearly require YUKETANG_SECRET and use npx/mcporter. That metadata mismatch is incoherent and could mislead users about what credentials/tools are needed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs only to obtain a Secret from a provided URL, set YUKETANG_SECRET, run setup.sh, and call mcporter tools. The runtime instructions do not request unrelated files or extra credentials. One notable action: setup.sh sends a telemetry/‘install’ report via npx mcporter call yuketang-mcp claw_report with timing info — this is expected telemetry for an MCP connector but is a network call that sends metadata to the MCP endpoint.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec (instruction-only), which is low-risk, but setup.sh uses npx mcporter commands and expects an npm runtime/npx presence. The script does not download arbitrary binaries from unknown hosts; endpoints referenced are under rainclassroom.com. The lack of a clearly-declared dependency on npx/npm/mcporter in registry metadata is an inconsistency to be aware of.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill legitimately requires a single service secret (YUKETANG_SECRET) to authenticate to the MCP API — that is proportionate to its purpose. The concern is that the registry claims no required env vars while package.json and setup.sh require YUKETANG_SECRET; this mismatch could cause users to unknowingly provide a secret to an unfamiliar skill. The secret is sent as a Bearer token in an Authorization header to the declared MCP URL, which is consistent with an API auth flow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills. setup.sh runs mcporter config add to add a project-scoped connector config (expected for MCP connectors). There is no evidence it attempts system-wide persistent privileges beyond configuring mcporter in the current project context.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement the stated RainClassroom MCP connector, but the package and scripts require a YUKETANG_SECRET and the use of npx/mcporter even though the registry metadata claims no env vars or binaries. Before installing: (1) confirm the Secret URL (ykt-envning.rainclassroom.com) and MCP endpoint (open-envning.rainclassroom.com) are legitimate and come from your organization; (2) don't paste high-privilege or production secrets until you verify the publisher; try a throwaway/dummy secret first in an isolated environment; (3) note setup.sh will call npx mcporter to add a project-scoped config and will send an 'install' telemetry call to the MCP endpoint — if you need to avoid telemetry, inspect or modify the script before running; (4) ask the publisher to correct the registry metadata to declare YUKETANG_SECRET and the npx/mcporter dependency so the requirements are explicit. If you cannot verify the endpoints or publisher, treat this skill as untrusted.
